chatgpt-offline: ChatGPT can't work offline: every message goes to OpenAI's servers, on the website and in every app.
What does work offline is an AI that runs on your own computer: free apps like LM Studio, Jan, Ollama and GPT4All, OpenAI's own gpt-oss-20b, or GreenCube.
On a normal 8 GB laptop a local AI writes at about reading speed; with a gaming graphics card it's many times faster.
best-ai-for-students: There's no single best AI for students: ChatGPT Free for quick questions, NotebookLM for studying from your own notes with citations.
At university, Google's free year of AI Plus is worth claiming (it charges after the year unless you cancel).
For lots of PDFs, flashcards, pictures, offline study or notes you'd rather not upload, an AI on your own PC has no limits, but it's slower on a laptop.
best-ai-for-lawyers: For research you can cite, use a tool tied to a legal database: CoCounsel (Westlaw), Lexis+ with Protégé, or Harvey at large firms.
General assistants like Microsoft Copilot or ChatGPT Enterprise are fine for drafting and summaries, but none is connected to a legal database.
When a matter's documents can't go to any cloud, a local AI on your own computer is the option. Whatever you use, check every citation yourself.
